rich_summary: Kunti, having invoked the sun god Surya through a sacred mantra, finds herself unable to dismiss him when he appears and demands union. Torn between fear of his curse and the shame and social ruin that would follow if she obeyed him, she struggles internally with duty, reputation, and innocence. Surya argues that no sin will touch her and promises she will remain a virgin afterward; he also foretells that their son will be mighty and born with divine armor and earrings. Reluctantly consenting, Kunti receives Surya through his yogic power and faints. She later gives birth secretly to a radiant child—Karna—already bearing the celestial armor and earrings. Afraid of disgrace as an unmarried mother, she sorrowfully places the infant in a sealed basket and sets him afloat on the river, praying for his safety. The episode establishes Karna’s divine origin and the tragic secrecy that shapes his fate.

top_scenes.scene_text: The radiant sun god Surya appearing before the young Kunti in a chamber filled with golden light as she pleads with trembling hands.
Surya, blazing with celestial radiance, touching Kunti’s navel with yogic power as divine light fills the room and she collapses fainting onto her bed.
Kunti weeping at the riverbank at dawn as she sets a wicker basket carrying the newborn Karna—glowing with golden armor and earrings—onto the flowing water.
